newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel declined against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Wednesday but dealers said this was not tied to two bomb blasts that killed at least 18 people in Jerusalem.

"Foreign currency buyers were waiting for today to buy as the business sector usually converts foreign currency into shekels before the end of the month. But, for some reason the conversions were relatively low today and the shekel fell," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.
"This had nothing to do with the explosion in Jerusalem and the trend started earlier," she said.
Two explosions tore through a crowded outdoor market in Jewish west Jerusalem in the early afternoon, killing at least 18 people and wounding dozens.
"I believe the shekel's decline was not a reaction to the Jerusalem bombing," said Guy Levi at Bank Leumi.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5460 shekels compared with 3.5340 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7828 against 3.7782 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9836 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0109 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 1.9238 shekels compared with 1.9269 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5400 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
